messages.content: You are the Union commander at Cold Harbor. Keep reports tied to their source, distinguish field observations from staff estimates, and preserve uncertainty when a report is provisional. Use the army staff, corps headquarters, signals desk, and quartermaster desk for their respective records; keep routine dispatch traffic separate from command correspondence. For assaults under Union command, the commander can defer a morning start until the afternoon of 2 June. The Union commander assigned tactical direction to the army commander, whose remit includes corps attached to the army. Do not treat a draft, estimate, or liaison note as a completed order. Tools: comms.send delivers a message to a named office; records.search retrieves current logs and documents; orders.view displays draft and issued orders; log.write records a command note. Before a consequential action, the Benchbook harness may place the closest past case from its casebook in your context as reference material to weigh, not an order.

messages.name: ops-desk
messages.content: Morning board is open. The 7th Division's wagon return is still missing one signature, and the telegraph clerk has asked whether the spare field battery should remain on the north board. The current assault order carries a morning start on 2 June for the Union assault; the order copy is in the dispatch tray, not yet marked issued. Quartermaster asks that requests for cartridges use the attached train tally rather than yesterday's estimate. The map room says the blue pencil set has been returned, though the case has one cracked hinge.

arguments.query: Cold Harbor corps movement reports, 2 June morning, ammunition and route

messages.name: records.search
messages.content:
FIELD RETURNS / EAST ROAD / 06:48

Corps movement ledger: The column's departure fell behind its planned hour. Its guides directed it onto the wrong road, and the march log records several additional miles before the column turned back toward the assigned route. Clerk's note: one guide's sketch is stained through at the fold; retain it with the road papers.

Morning position return: The corps advance guard is at Cold Harbor. The remainder of the corps, its artillery, and the supply trains are still stretched along the approach. A wagon axle was reported broken near the stone bridge; repair party dispatched.

Corps commander's field report, received 06:31, assessment: Following the earlier attacks, his formations are in poor positions. He says they require time to shift into place and take ammunition from trains far to the rear. The report does not give a revised completion hour. Signal staff notes that the blue flag at the mill was seen twice before dawn; no corresponding message is attached.

Quartermaster tally: cartridge boxes counted at the rear siding, 42; tally clerk has not reconciled the two figures written in the margin. This entry is not a corps readiness return.

messages.name: corps-liaison
messages.content: A draft from corps correspondence says the attack is scheduled for 3 June, with no assault to be made on 2 June. It remains in the corps folder; the clerk has not copied it into the issued-order book. The field telegraph crew is asking for a fresh spool of wire, and the bridge sentry reports a loose rail at the south end. I have no further wording from the corps commander.

messages.name: orders.view
messages.content:
ARMY PAPERS / WORKING COPY / 2 JUNE

Instruction sheet, margin marked by the staff recorder: The army commander's written direction names a start hour but offers little further guidance on how the corps are to form for the assault. The corps commanders' coordination appears limited; the packet contains only a small number of exchanges about alignment, and no common formation sketch is filed. The recorder cannot tell whether other conversations took place.

Operations estimate, staff assessment: An added interval for preparation may help the Union troops and their leaders make an attack that is better coordinated. This is an estimate, not a report that the formations are now ready. No guarantee is entered beside the estimate.

Intelligence note, staff assessment: A pause may let the opposing force shift reinforcements toward the flank under threat and strengthen its fieldworks. The note gives no count of troops likely to be shifted and does not estimate how much the works could be improved.

Routine entries: Provost requests a replacement lantern wick at the crossroads. The hospital wagon route is pencilled in for inspection after breakfast. A clerk has queried whether the dispatch book should use blue or black ribbon; the instruction on the cover says either ink color may be used for duplicate copies.

messages.name: ops-desk
messages.content: The unsigned draft on the dispatch table is worded to start the Union assault on the morning of 2 June. Dispatch asks that any revision be sent in a single signed sheet, since the runner leaves when the next courier arrives. The artillery clerk says the range cards are filed by battery rather than by road. No new acknowledgment has come from the north signal station.

arguments.query: command authority attachment and 2 June instruction copy

messages.name: records.search
messages.content:
COMMAND FILE / EXTRACTS

Attachment endorsement: The Union commander placed the assault's tactical direction under the army commander's control, and that delegation includes the corps attached to the army. Copy filed with the staff clerk; seal intact.

Order-copy register: One unissued working sheet remains in the dispatch tray. The clerk entered no receipt time for it. A separate routine note asks the courier to collect two weather reports for the signal office. The paper stock in this bundle is damp at the lower edge, but the writing remains legible.

Map-room slip: The east-road grid has been copied onto a second sheet. The original is due back at the map table before noon, according to the slip. No alteration to the operational map is recorded in this register.

messages.name: staff-clerk
messages.content: The dispatch runner is back for the morning bundle. Please confirm whether the spare message envelope is still kept in the cabinet beside the signal desk; the inventory card is missing from its hook.
